The Perfect Crime or a Perfect Lie? The Shocking Trial of Rebecca Fenton.

On Super Bowl Sunday in 2008, Rebecca Fenton made a frantic 911 call claiming she returned home from the gym to find her husband, Larry Fenton, lying in a pool of blood. The wealthy pharmaceutical representative had been shot five times in what initially looked like a brutal home invasion and robbery. But as investigators looked past the surface, the "grieving wife" narrative began to unravel.

Despite a prenuptial agreement that would leave her with almost nothing in a divorce, Larry's death meant a payout of over $1 million. For six years, the case stalled due to a lack of physical evidence—until a cold case detective stepped in. Uncovering staged crime scene details, suspicious 911 call indicators, a hidden murder weapon, and a terrifying confession made to an ex-boyfriend, the state built a powerful circumstantial case.

In this gripping true crime deep dive, we explore the dual realities of Rebecca Fenton: Is she the victim of a catastrophic miscarriage of justice, or a calculating sociopath who managed to look a reporter in the eye and spin an intricate web of lies? Watch the evidence unfold, including the jaw-dropping moment her own biological mother breaks her silence to reveal what she truly believes happened that fateful day.

snippet.title: Is This The Most Dangerous Country To Report The Truth?
snippet.description:
Through conversations with reporters, editors, cartoonists, and Kurdish war correspondents, the documentary reveals a country where journalism has become dangerous work. Newsrooms face political pressure, self-censorship, police raids, lawsuits, and public intimidation — yet many journalists continue speaking out despite the risks.

The film explores:

- The collapse of press freedom in Turkey
- Fear, censorship, and political polarization in the media
- Journalists losing jobs for refusing government pressure
- Satire and social media as forms of resistance
- The blurred line between journalism and activism
- The personal cost of telling uncomfortable truths

At the heart of the story is a difficult question:
Can journalists remain neutral when democracy itself is under pressure?

This episode features interviews with Turkish journalists, editors, satirists from Leman, Kurdish reporters, and media critics from across the political spectrum.

snippet.title: Who Killed Little Gregory Villemin? | The Curse of the Vologne | Ep 1
snippet.description:
On October 16, 1984, the peaceful Vologne Valley in Eastern France became the backdrop for one of the most harrowing and mysterious crimes in European history. Four-year-old Gregory Villemin was kidnapped from his front yard and later found drowned in the frozen waters of the Vologne River, his hands and feet loosely bound with a weaver's knot—the signature of a local.

But the horror didn't start there. For three agonizing years, the Villemin family had been terrorized by a malicious, anonymous harasser known as "Le Corbeau" (The Crow), who weaponized telephone calls and letters to expose dark family secrets and jealousy over Jean-Marie Villemin’s promotion to factory foreman.

In this true crime documentary deep-dive, we unpack the first weeks of the investigation. From the claustrophobic law of silence in small-town France to the interconnected family trees of the Villemins, Jacobs, and Bolles, we examine how deep-seated envy led to the ultimate child sacrifice. Was it the estranged brother, Jackie? Or did the trail lead to Bernard Laroche?

Discover how a toxic spiral of jealousy, ancestral secrets, and an impenetrable wall of silence left a community frozen in fear—and a murder case unresolved to this day.

snippet.title: Evil Lives Here | One Gold SUV Connected a Trail of Shootings | American Documentary True Crime
snippet.description:
A woman driving to work saw a large SUV with its lights off. Minutes later, shotgun blasts tore through her car—and the same vehicle would soon become the clue detectives could not ignore.

This American true crime documentary follows a Los Angeles murder investigation that began with a survivor’s terrifying roadside attack and rapidly widened into a police hunt. Nicole fought to survive severe throat injuries, while families learned that loved ones—including Gloria Tovar—had been shot in a string of attacks linked by a gold or tan SUV and a shotgun. As detectives traced earlier freeway shootings, the pattern grew more alarming: victims appeared to have been targeted at random.

Police closed in on Alex Hernandez, then examined the SUV for the evidence that could connect separate crimes. The case explores the pressure of a fast-moving investigation, the anguish of victims’ families, and the determination of a survivor who chose to testify after losing her voice.

A gripping real crime case about a murder investigation, police evidence, and a trail of shootings across Los Angeles.

snippet.title: This 20-Year-Old Cold Case Is Uncovered! | Sensing Murder New Zealand | Season 5 Episode 3
snippet.description:
Sensing Murder is a true crime documentary series that revisits real unsolved murder cases from New Zealand and Australia. Each episode focuses on a different victim, telling their story through emotional interviews with family members, friends, and former partners, painting a picture of who they were before their lives were tragically cut short. Viewers get an intimate look at the victim's personality, dreams, and the final days leading up to their death.

The series then dives into the crime itself: the investigation, the evidence gathered, the suspects questioned, and the theories police pursued at the time. Many of these cases were never solved, leaving families without answers for decades, and often facing unfair speculation or media distortion about their loved one's character along the way.

In the final segment of each episode, two psychic mediums work independently, with no prior information about the victim, in an attempt to connect with their spirit. They share what they sense about the victim's life, the events surrounding their death, and any details that might offer new clues. For grieving families still searching for closure, Sensing Murder offers a unique blend of true crime investigation and the unexplained, keeping these unsolved cases, and the hope for justice, alive.

snippet.title: Najpierw skatował niemowlę. Potem przyniósł kwiaty kobiecie, którą zabił | Dokument Kryminalny
snippet.description:
Ray Clark na początku wyglądał jak idealny partner. Był czarujący, dobrze ubrany i potrafił sprawić, że Andrea Bill uwierzyła w jego miłość. Z czasem pojawiły się jednak telefony bez końca, obsesja, groźby, kwiaty i wiadomość, której Andrea nigdy nie zapomniała: „Śmierć jest blisko”.

Kiedy Andrea zaszła w ciążę, Ray zaczął pokazywać swoją prawdziwą twarz. Groził dziecku, próbował zastraszać matkę, a później brutalnie skrzywdził niemowlę. Mimo ostrzeżeń i interwencji Ray nadal był na wolności.

Po rozstaniu Andrea próbowała ostrzec kolejną kobietę, Tawanę, która nie chciała uwierzyć w to, do czego Ray był zdolny. Niedługo później Ray przyniósł jej kwiaty. Gdy weszła do domu, aby włożyć je do wazonu, została zastrzelona.

To Dokument Kryminalny o przemocy domowej, obsesji, śmierci niewinnych osób i mężczyźnie, który przez lata ukrywał się za pozorami miłości.

snippet.title: Krew była wszędzie w łazience. Księgowy zaginionej pary zabrał prawdę do grobu | Archiwum zbrodni
snippet.description:
Elizabeth „Liz” i John Calvert byli właścicielami Harbour Town Yacht Basin na Hilton Head Island w Karolinie Południowej. Byli lubianym małżeństwem, planowali wspólną przyszłość i prowadzili dobrze znany biznes. Wszystko zmieniło się, gdy Liz zaczęła sprawdzać dokumenty finansowe firmy.

W księgach pojawiły się nieprawidłowości, których nie potrafiła wyjaśnić. Podejrzenia prowadziły do byłego księgowego, Dennisa Gerwinga. 3 marca 2008 roku Liz i John spotkali się z nim, aby porozmawiać o finansach. Po tym spotkaniu oboje zniknęli bez śladu.

Śledczy odkryli sprzeczne zeznania, wyłączony telefon, zakup plastrów, lateksowych rękawiczek oraz trzech dużych plandek przemysłowych. Kilka dni później Dennis Gerwing został znaleziony martwy w łazience pełnej krwi. Jego śmierć uznano za samobójstwo, lecz nie zostawił jasnej odpowiedzi na pytanie, co stało się z Elizabeth i Johnem.

This documentary explores the hidden side of the modern global illicit trade network and how it has evolved into a highly sophisticated and nearly invisible system.

Unlike older eras where major criminal figures operated openly and attracted global attention, today’s structures function in a far more discreet and complex way. The individuals behind these networks rarely appear in the spotlight. Instead, they operate through layers of intermediaries, legal businesses, and international logistics systems that make detection extremely difficult.

The film takes a deep look into how these covert networks are built, how they expand across continents, and how they manage to remain hidden within everyday global commerce. It highlights the transformation of organized crime from visible hierarchies into decentralized and highly adaptive systems.

Special attention is given to the methods used to move illegal goods across borders, the financial structures used to hide profits, and the way legitimate industries can sometimes be exploited as cover. The documentary also shows how international enforcement agencies attempt to track and dismantle these hidden operations, often facing significant challenges due to their complexity and scale.

At its core, this documentary raises an important question: how does something so large operate so quietly in a world that is more connected and monitored than ever before?

snippet.title: The Unsolved Case Resurfaces | Sensing Murder New Zealand | Season 5 Episode 1
snippet.description:
Sensing Murder is a true crime documentary series that revisits real unsolved murder cases from New Zealand and Australia. Each episode focuses on a different victim, telling their story through emotional interviews with family members, friends, and former partners, painting a picture of who they were before their lives were tragically cut short. Viewers get an intimate look at the victim's personality, dreams, and the final days leading up to their death.

The series then dives into the crime itself: the investigation, the evidence gathered, the suspects questioned, and the theories police pursued at the time. Many of these cases were never solved, leaving families without answers for decades, and often facing unfair speculation or media distortion about their loved one's character along the way.

In the final segment of each episode, two psychic mediums work independently, with no prior information about the victim, in an attempt to connect with their spirit. They share what they sense about the victim's life, the events surrounding their death, and any details that might offer new clues. For grieving families still searching for closure, Sensing Murder offers a unique blend of true crime investigation and the unexplained, keeping these unsolved cases, and the hope for justice, alive.
